prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- Police have arrested a man in the killing of Auburn University freshman Lauren Burk, who died this week, according to the Auburn, Alabama, assistant police chief. Courtney Larrell Lockhart, 23, of Smiths, Alabama, is charged with capital murder during a kidnapping, capital murder during a robbery, and capital murder during an attempted rape, Tommy Dawson said Saturday. The Phenix City Police Department took Lockhart into custody on Friday, police said. Phenix City is about 35 miles southeast of Auburn. Burk, 18, from Marietta, Georgia, was found shot on North College Street, a few miles north of campus, on Tuesday night. She died later at a hospital. Minutes after police responded to the call reporting an injured person and found Burk, they found a car -- which turned out to be Burk's -- on fire in a campus parking lot. Dawson told reporters Friday that authorities think gasoline or another accelerant was used to ignite Burk's car, and police were investigating whether a gas can found in downtown Auburn was connected. Police want to investigate every possible lead, Dawson said. Authorities were still on patrol in the east Alabama campus, he said. The university's Web site said a campus-wide memorial service will be held Monday. The site carried a message from Burk's father, James, which said: "The Burk family was so proud to have Lauren as an Auburn University student. We want to extend our deepest gratitude and appreciation for Auburn University, the city of Auburn and the Auburn Police Department. We feel very close to your community. We appreciate what everyone is doing for us and Lauren." Also on Friday, police released pictures of a 2001 Honda Civic similar to Burk's car. Authorities asked anyone who thinks they might have seen the car on Tuesday to contact them. Police are continuing to interview people, Dawson said. A student at the University of North Carolina in Chapel Hill -- Eve Carson, 22, of Athens, Georgia -- was also shot to death this week, on early Wednesday. Authorities in Chapel Hill said Friday they had been in contact with Auburn police but did not believe the two cases were connected.   Watch CNN's Nancy Grace discuss the two killings of college women from Georgia » . Burk's family, in a statement read Friday to reporters by family friend Kathy Singleton, expressed their gratitude for the thoughts and prayers offered, but asked for privacy "so that they may grieve for their loss as well as celebrate Lauren's life." Those wishing to honor Burk could do so by donating to her favorite charities, Singleton said -- The Invisible Child and the American Kidney Foundation. Donations can be made at any Wachovia Bank to the Lauren Burk Memorial Fund. E-mail to a friend .

Courtney Larrell Lockhart, 23, of Smiths, Alabama, faces three charges: capital murder committed during a kidnapping, capital murder committed during a robbery, and capital murder committed during an attempted rape, Assistant Police Chief Tommy Dawson announced Saturday.

According to police, officers with the Phenix City Police Department apprehended Lockhart on Friday. Phenix City lies approximately 35 miles southeast of Auburn.

Burk, an 18-year-old from Marietta, Georgia, was discovered Tuesday night with a gunshot wound along North College Street, several miles north of the university campus. She was transported to a hospital, where she later died.

On Friday, investigators also distributed photographs of a 2001 Honda Civic resembling Burk’s vehicle. They asked anyone who might have seen the car Tuesday to get in touch with authorities. Dawson said police were continuing to conduct interviews.

Another college student from Georgia was fatally shot during the same week. Eve Carson, 22, of Athens, Georgia, attended the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill and was killed early Wednesday. Chapel Hill authorities said Friday that they had communicated with Auburn police but did not think the two deaths were connected. CNN’s Nancy Grace discussed the killings of the two Georgia college students.

Singleton said those interested in honoring Burk could contribute to two charities she particularly supported: The Invisible Child and the American Kidney Foundation. Contributions to the Lauren Burk Memorial Fund could be made at any Wachovia Bank.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize everything known about Lauren Burk’s death and the arrest in Auburn, Alabama, while also mentioning the unrelated killing of UNC student Eve Carson.
counterfactuals.output:
### Lauren Burk’s killing

- **Lauren Ashley Burk**, 18, was a freshman from Marietta, Georgia, at **Auburn University**.
- On the evening of **March 4, 2008**, a motorist found her wounded beside **Alabama Highway 147**, near Auburn’s campus. She had been shot and later died at **East Alabama Medical Center**.
- Around the same time, Burk’s **black Honda Civic** was discovered burning in an Auburn campus parking lot. Investigators concluded that she had been abducted while entering or near her car, robbed, and shot while trying to escape.
- Prosecutors later said the assailant forced Burk to withdraw or surrender money and attempted to sexually assault her. Burk fled and was shot in the back.

### Arrest and prosecution

- **Courtney Larod Lockhart**, then 23 and an Iraq War veteran from the Smiths Station/Phenix City area, was arrested on **March 7, 2008**, three days after the killing.
- The arrest followed a police pursuit in **Phenix City, Alabama**, roughly 35 miles southeast of Auburn. Investigators connected him to Burk’s case through evidence recovered after the arrest, including a handgun later tied to the shooting, and through his statements to police.
- Lockhart admitted abducting and robbing Burk but disputed parts of the prosecution’s account, including intent. He was charged with capital murder because the killing occurred during crimes including kidnapping and robbery.
- In 2010, a jury convicted him of **capital murder** and unanimously recommended **life imprisonment without parole**. The trial judge used Alabama’s then-legal judicial-override system to impose a **death sentence** instead.
- After years of appeals and litigation over his representation and sentencing, Lockhart’s death sentence was vacated. He was ultimately resentenced to **life without the possibility of parole**.

### Unrelated killing of Eve Carson

The case drew additional national attention because **Eve Marie Carson**, 22, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill’s student-body president, was abducted, robbed, and shot to death in Chapel Hill on **March 5, 2008**, one day after Burk was attacked. Despite the close timing and the fact that both victims were college students abducted in connection with their cars, authorities said the crimes were **unrelated**. Carson’s killers, **Demario Atwater and Laurence Lovette Jr.**, were prosecuted separately.

Authorities said the evidence indicated Burk was abducted and robbed. Dawson urged anyone who saw Burk, her vehicle or suspicious activity around the university at the time of the crime to contact investigators.

In a statement, Burk’s family remembered her as a loving daughter, sister and friend whose life had been filled with promise. The family also expressed gratitude for the support it received from the Auburn community, law enforcement officers and people in Burk’s hometown.

A memorial fund was established in Burk’s name through Wachovia Bank. The family said contributions would be directed to charitable causes that were important to her, allowing her commitment to helping others to continue after her death.

The family asked that donations be made to the memorial fund in lieu of flowers.
